answer: An agent market can let agents named vine, plume, and zephyr trade freely but require each voting identity to lock a fixed bond in escrow. The same deposit cannot back two identities, and it stays locked until the voting and challenge periods end. An attacker seeking 1,000 votes must therefore tie up 1,000 bonds at once, bearing the cost of borrowing that capital or taking it away from other uses even if every bond is returned.
